title: HTTP Requests with Net::HTTP
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of http requests with net::http in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply http requests with net::http in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to tls verification and error handling and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn HTTP Requests with Net::HTTP through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding http requests with net::http helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: HTTP Requests with Net::HTTP helps you reason about get, post, and other methods. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: GET, POST, and other methods. Then connect it to Headers and bodies. The remaining syllabus points—Status codes and timeouts, TLS verification and error handling—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: HTTP Requests with Net::HTTP
content_blocks.code:
require "net/http"
uri = URI("https://example.com")
request = Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri)
puts request.method

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports http requests with net::http. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for http requests with net::http using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (TLS verification and error handling), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain http requests with net::http, identify its place in files, input/output, and the standard library, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
